claim: selectionRegion ignores consuming ancestors, so a consumed (never drawn) child yields a selection export region

triage.scenario: select an operand of a boolean/compound node (reachable by entering it: `enteredGroup.isEnterable` allows consumesChildren). The operand is never painted on its own; `sceneContentBounds` excludes such nodes (`consumed`, contentBounds.ts:36). selectionRegion returns the operand's full drawn box, so an intersect/subtract result exports with a region framing ink that is not there (or a result that draws nothing exports as non-null). Expected: the operand treated like other undrawn nodes (or mapped to its consuming ancestor).

claim: regionRenderArgs draws the document but reads the background function from the shown scene
exportRegions throws synchronously when a format's `export` throws, though every other failure rejects
Dev 'unread option' warning is suppressed for an override of the same format id that reads different options

triage.scenario: `exportRegions(scene, r, 'png', { dpi: 2 })` warns once and records `png\0dpi`. A consumer then registers its own `png` format declaring `options: []` (or a different set), or disposes it and the built-in reappears; a later misspelled/unsupported `dpi` passed to the new format is never warned about, because the dedupe key is the id, not the format object whose `options` decided the warning. Keyed by format (e.g. a WeakMap<ExportFormat, Set<string>>) each registration would warn for itself.
triage.cause: dedupe keyed by id rather than the format registered

claim: selectionRegion treats a zero-width or zero-height region as drawing something, so the PNG export then refuses it

triage.scenario: select only a straight horizontal (or vertical) path with no stroke, or any node whose drawn box is degenerate on one axis. `unionAabb` returns a box with `height: 0`, so `selectionRegion` returns a region rather than `null`, and `selectionRegionSource` does not raise its "draws nothing" error. `exportRegions(scene, selectionRegionsSource(ids), 'png')` then reaches `planPixelRender`, whose `checkPixelRenderRect` throws `renderSceneToPixels: sourceRect.height must be a positive finite number, got 0`. Expected: either `null` / the "draws nothing" error that the doc promises for a selection drawing nothing, or a region the formats accept.
triage.cause: degenerate box not treated as empty

claim: selectionRegion boxes hidden nodes and annotation-layer nodes, which no export draws
selectionRegion omits the copies a selected container draws via copiesFromPose, so the exported crop cuts them off

triage.scenario: select a symmetry group (a container with `copiesFromPose`) and export the selection as PNG/SVG/PDF. `boxOf` answers `drawnAabbOf` of the group, which unions its members' boxes but never carries them through the copies (drawnBounds.ts `inkExtentsOf` has no copy step). The region is the original's box only, so every mirrored/rotated copy outside it is cut off. `sceneContentBounds` (core/canvas/contentBounds.ts:38-44) answers the same "what does this draw" question with `copiesWithin` and covers the copies — two answers to one decision.
triage.cause: copies not carried into selection bounds

claim: No selection region source: the README's selection export reads its bounds outside the revision it draws
selectionRegion measures `{ px }` strokes at scale 1, so an export at scale < 1 crops them
Strict PNG export validates the warmup plan's diagnostics, not the final plan's, so losses introduced after warmup go unreported
The registry's `background` is typed `string | null`, so exportRegions/exportPages cannot take the revision-read function every format accepts
shownIds recurses into children of a consumesChildren node on a hidden or annotation layer, counting ones the render walk never paints

triage.scenario: a boolean/compound node (`consumesChildren: true`) sits on a hidden layer (or an annotation layer) and is selected. `shown` replaces it with `doc.childrenOf(id).flatMap(shown)`, so its operands' boxes become the region, though the walk draws neither the node nor its operands (`buildSceneTree` gives a consuming node no children; `sceneContentBounds` contentBounds.ts:33 and `paintedMembers` drawnBounds.ts:108 both return [] here). Expected `null` / "draws nothing"; got a region over undrawn operands, exporting an empty or wrong image. The same "what does a hidden-layer node draw" rule is answered three ways.
